issues.description: Default turn_detection_mode flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED is a silent breaking change.
issues.detail: Every caller that didn't pin the value gets different runtime behavior after a patch upgrade. A changelog line is not a migration. Keep EXTERNAL as default and require opt-in, or label this loudly as breaking with a clear migration note and deprecation warning.

issues.description: Switching finalize trigger to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame silently breaks non-VAD callers.
issues.detail: The handler previously reacted to UserStoppedSpeakingFrame; it now only finalizes on the VAD-flavored frame. Callers driving turns manually or via custom endpointers lose finalization with no warning. Either accept both frame types, or state the new contract in code with a defensive route and test pinning which frame finalizes.

issues.description: TurnDetectionMode and EndOfUtteranceMode track the same fact in parallel with implicit mapping.
issues.detail: The public API toggles TurnDetectionMode while _enable_vad gates on EndOfUtteranceMode, with FIXED added to both. One concept (who owns endpointing) is stored in two places with an undocumented 1:1 mapping. Collapse to one source of truth and derive the rest, or at minimum comment the invariant explicitly.

issues.description: speech_segment_config is unconditionally overwritten, clobbering any prior value.
issues.detail: _prepare_config replaces the whole SpeechSegmentConfig object rather than mutating it. Any prior assignment or future-added field is silently lost. Prefer mutating the existing config, or only assign when split_sentences is explicitly set.

issues.description: Commented-out start_processing_metrics call was relocated rather than resolved.
issues.detail: The dead `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` line was moved within _handle_start_of_turn instead of being deleted or restored. Either the metric belongs there (uncomment with a reason) or it doesn't (delete). Relocated dead code signals an unanswered question about when a turn actually starts.

issues.description: split_sentences default is encoded in two places with ambiguous None semantics.
issues.detail: Declared as Optional[bool]=None on InputParams, then coerced via `params.split_sentences or False` at config time. The effective default is False but the type says None is meaningful. Pick a real bool with default False, or honor None as 'inherit upstream' — don't complect 'unset' with 'false'.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. Three independent changes — a new split_sentences parameter, a default flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED, and a switch of finalize trigger from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame — ship as one diff and together constitute a silent breaking change for existing callers. The core concept of "who owns end-of-turn detection" is spread across two parallel enums and a derived boolean with no stated invariant. Smaller hygiene issues (unconditional config overwrite, relocated dead-comment metric call, ambiguous Optional[bool] default) compound the readability cost. Split the patch, preserve the old default or shout about the break, and unify the endpointing-owner concept to one source of truth.
